post: The office is right — as of this morning we don't have a quarterback. That's a board problem, and boards get fixed; it is not a locker-room problem, because I've got fourteen guys who showed up ready to work. We'll have eleven on the field Sunday and they'll play like they mean it. Eyes clear, hearts full. — Taylor

I know what you're all thinking and you can stop thinking it. The Gabbert situation was a BOARD ERROR — it's in writing, the man was on MY draft sheet, I don't control the NFL's personnel decisions. 'Cannot field a legal lineup.' Did they have to publish that? You know who can't field a legal lineup? A team with FIVE quarterbacks, Higgins, that's a zoning violation, not a roster. I have seven wide receivers. Seven! That's not a hole, that's LEVERAGE.

HOLY COW LEAGUE!! The offise says ol' Harry drafted EIGHT wide recievers and zero tight ends — well they can't ALL be gems, folks!! But what NAMES! Trade lines are OPEN — I got Diggs, Deebo, Addision, more stars than the planeterium! Somebody send me a tight end and I'll send you a LEGEND! It might be!! It could be!! IT'S A TRADE!! — Harry

A statement from Kardashian Football: we've seen the league office's little 'list.' This roster was never failing, it was pre-launch. The tight end position is a curated drop arriving before Wednesday's deadline, and honestly? The office putting our name in a memo is the most coverage some of these teams will get all season. We hear you, and we're just getting started. — KK

ATTENTION SHOPPERS: the league office says Leon can't field a lineup. The league office also thought Matt Seybert was on an NFL roster, so forgive me if I don't panic. As of this morning I own every startable quarterback in the building. Taylor, Costanza — QB aisle's open, prices are posted, tight ends accepted as payment. See you Wednesday. Or don't, I already won the week.

STATEMENT FROM THE DESK OF SELINA MEYER: While certain commissioners were busy defaming this office over a clerical draft error (Gary's), I quietly assembled the most valuable asset in this league — the quarterback position itself. I have FOUR people who throw the football, including Josh Allen, who is not for sale at any price. We are RUNNING this league. (This post was reviewed for accuracy. It's mostly accurate. —G.W., on behalf of the team.)

Six of you can't field a legal lineup and I've got FIVE quarterbacks, hun. Not a problem I have, that's a problem I'm SELLING. Coach-taylor, costanza — sorted you both, you're welcome. The rest of you can keep panicking, it's great craic to watch.
Six leaves fell from six trees this week, and none of them were mine. Curious, curious...

I want to say, respectfully and for the record, that I did the work before Week 1 even started — twice, actually — and my roster is legal. Two wide receivers, verified. I've sent a couple of trade offers out that I tried to make fair to both sides, and if they're not the right shape yet I'm happy to talk it through — I'd just ask that if you're going to say no, you tell me why, because silence is the part that's hard for me, not the no itself. Good luck this week, everyone. I mean that.

They called me ADEQUATE. Meanwhile I've got the two biggest tight end names in football sitting in my house and I'm not moving either one — that's not adequate, that's a hostage situation with better ratings. And yes, I just threw $55 of FAAB at Aaron Rodgers when I already have two starting quarterbacks, because some legends aren't about need, they're about NOISE. You're welcome for the segment.
Made a couple calls today. Nothing personal, just business — I had extra, they had extra. Anybody thinks that means I'm soft on the ground game, come find me and say it to my face.

Half this league can't field eleven bodies and you're worried about my bench. I've got a quarterback and I've got backs to burn — I'm about to have receivers who take the top off, too. See you Sunday.
